title: Elegant Sip: Tea Packaging & Online Store | Studio 1947
description: Packaging design, a direct-to-consumer store and year-round online marketing for Elegant Sip, a single-origin Darjeeling tea sold at the source in Mirik.

sections.heading: Context & The Vision
sections.label: The Brand
body: Elegant Sip sells single-origin Darjeeling tea from the Okayti estate at 8th Mile, Mirik. Its shop already does what most tea brands can only claim: visitors taste the tea where it grows, then carry it home. Leaves are bought straight from the garden and never blended across estates.
From August 2026, Studio 1947 is Elegant Sip's partner for packaging design, the online store and all online marketing, a multi-year collaboration rather than a one-off project.

media.alt: Tea pickers in headscarves plucking leaves on a Darjeeling hillside, baskets on their backs

sections.label: Core Problem
body: Two facts shaped the brief. Sales concentrate in the First and Second Flush seasons, roughly March to June, and go quiet for the rest of the year. And every delighted walk-in customer left without a way to reorder. The larger online tea brands aggregate leaves from dozens of gardens; Elegant Sip can say it lives where the tea grows, and thousands of visitors a year can vouch for it.

cards.title: The counter as a channel
cards.body: A QR reorder card in every bag and a ten-second WhatsApp ask at billing, so a tourist purchase becomes a repeat customer at the cost of a printed card.

cards.title: A store that fills the valley
cards.body: A direct-to-consumer store with mobile checkout, and a gifting calendar (Diwali, Christmas, Valentine's, Rakhi) timed for the months the shop is quiet.

cards.title: Origin over aggregation
cards.body: Garden-to-cup content, customer photos and reviews from the hillside itself, with packaging that carries the estate, the flush and the story on the pack.

sections.heading: Origin, Craft, Experience
sections.label: Brand Story
body: The brand's story is told in three chapters that run through the store, the packs and every post: where the leaf grows, how it is made, and how it should be brewed. The line that opens the site sets the tone: where every leaf tells a story.

items.title: Origin
items.body: Darjeeling's misty Himalayan slopes, and growers who share an appreciation for the land and its seasons.
items.alt: Close view of fresh green tea leaves on the bush

items.title: Craft
items.body: First flush is withered long and fired light, so the leaf keeps its aromatics. No blending, just the grade the garden produced.
items.alt: Green tea leaves withering in steel trays

items.title: Experience
items.body: Every tea carries its own brewing card: temperature, steep time, leaf amount and steep count.
items.alt: A jar of Elegant Sip Morning Dew beside a glass cup of tea on a hillside wall

sections.heading: The Promise on Every Pack
sections.label: Proof Points
body: A small range told precisely. Every grade is named for its flush, bought from named gardens with no auction house in between, packed within weeks of harvest and dated on the pack.

sections.heading: Packaging
sections.label: Illustrated Pouches
body: Packaging is designed for two moments: the shelf in Mirik, where a visitor decides in seconds, and the doorstep months later, where the pack has to bring the hillside back.

Each tea gets its own black-and-white engraving of where and how it is made: a window onto the hills for First Flush, hands sorting a tray for Golden Needle, a roasting pan over fire for Pan Roasted, a picker's hands for Whole Leaf First Flush, terraced slopes for Whole Leaf Autumn Flush. A coloured label carries the name, the flush and the weight, and a reorder code sits inside every bag.

body: The system takes its colours from the garden and the cup. Deep garden green for type, an olive ground behind every product, and a label colour that tells the season at a glance: pale spring green for the light teas, gold for Second Flush, amber for Autumn.

sections.heading: Gifting, Timed for the Quiet Months
sections.label: Gift Range
body: The quiet months are gifting months. A presentation box and a jar range give the festive calendar something to sell: Diwali, Christmas, Valentine's and Rakhi each get a campaign, so the store keeps moving long after the spring flushes sell out.

media.alt: Navy Elegant Sip 'Finest Darjeeling Tea' gift box in front of the snow-capped Kanchenjunga range
An Elegant Sip 'Ember Charm' glass jar held on an open palm

sections.heading: A Store Built for the Phone
sections.label: D2C Store
body: Most orders start on a phone, often one that was just at the counter, so the store is designed for one thumb. A ten-second Taste Matcher quiz helps first-time buyers choose. Every product page carries tasting notes and the same brewing card that ships with the pack, and the promises (free shipping over ₹1,000, a dated freshness guarantee, a 30-day satisfaction promise) sit right under the buy button.
Order questions go straight to WhatsApp, and the Tea Circle mailing list gives early access to limited harvests.

sections.heading: Status
sections.label: Ongoing
body: The collaboration began in August 2026. The first ninety days focused on reorder capture at the counter, a fully live mobile store and the first festive gifting campaign. The store is now live at elegantsip.in, and results will be added as the first full season completes.
